subject: Religious and Moral Education
source: RELIGIOUS AND MORAL EDUCATION CURRICULUM FOR PRIMARY SCHOOLS (BASIC I - 6), September 2019
teacher_guidance: Read questions aloud to learners where necessary. Accept verbal and demonstrative answers in English or a familiar local language. Assess knowledge of the three major religions respectfully and objectively, without evaluating personal beliefs.

indicators.objective: Name the three main types of worship in Ghana.
indicators.content_standard_as_printed: B1.2.1.1. Demonstrate the understanding of religious worship
indicators.strand: Religious Practices and their Moral Implications
indicators.sub_strand: Religious Worship in the Three Major Religions in Ghana

skills.description: Name Christian worship, Islamic worship, and Traditional worship as the three main types of worship in Ghana.
Identify pictures, media, or descriptions showing each of the three main types of religious worship in Ghana.
Demonstrate respect and role-play respectful acts associated with the three types of worship in Ghana.

misconceptions: Confusing prayer postures between Christian, Islamic, and Traditional worship
Believing only one religion exists in Ghana
Assuming traditional worship does not exist or is not recognised as one of the three main religions

questions.stem: How many main types of religious worship are named in our lesson for Ghana?
hints: Count Christian, Islamic, and Traditional worship.
questions.explanation: The curriculum specifies three main types of worship in Ghana: Christian, Islamic, and Traditional.

distractor_misconceptions.0: Thinking only one religion exists in Ghana
distractor_misconceptions.1: Leaving out one of the three main religions

questions.stem: Which of these is one of the three main types of worship in Ghana?
hints: Think about church and the Bible.
questions.explanation: Christian worship is one of the three main types of religious worship in Ghana taught in the curriculum.

distractor_misconceptions.1: Confusing buying food with religious worship
distractor_misconceptions.2: Confusing everyday school activities with religious worship
distractor_misconceptions.3: Confusing a sports game with religious worship

questions.stem: Which type of worship is practiced by Muslims in Ghana?
hints: Muslims worship in Islam.
questions.explanation: Muslims practice Islamic worship, which is one of the three main types of worship in Ghana.

questions.stem: Along with Christian worship and Islamic worship, name the third main type of worship in Ghana.
hints: It is the indigenous religion handed down by our ancestors.
questions.explanation: The three main religions in Ghana are Christianity, Islam, and African Traditional Religion. Therefore, Traditional worship is the third.
questions.misconception: Assuming traditional worship is not one of the three main types in Ghana

questions.stem: Which group lists the three main types of worship in Ghana correctly?
hints: Look for the three religions recognized in Ghana.
questions.explanation: Christian worship, Islamic worship, and Traditional worship are the three main types in Ghana.

distractor_misconceptions.1: Confusing school skills with religious worship
distractor_misconceptions.2: Confusing physical play with religious worship
distractor_misconceptions.3: Confusing times of day with types of religious worship

questions.stem: Kwame sees people singing hymns and praying inside a church. Which type of worship is this?
hints: Singing hymns in church is Christian practice.
questions.explanation: Worshipping in a church with hymns and Christian prayers is Christian worship.

distractor_misconceptions.0: Confusing church worship with mosque worship
distractor_misconceptions.2: Confusing church worship with shrine worship
distractor_misconceptions.3: Confusing church with general school gathering

questions.stem: Fatima sees worshippers bowing down and prostrating on prayer mats facing the Ka'bah. Which worship is this?
hints: Praying on mats with prostrations is practiced in Islam.
questions.explanation: Bowing and prostrating on prayer mats (Salat) is an act of Islamic worship.

distractor_misconceptions.0: Confusing Islamic prayer postures with traditional worship
distractor_misconceptions.1: Confusing Islamic prayer postures with Christian prayer
distractor_misconceptions.3: Mistaking prayer postures for physical exercise

questions.stem: Your teacher shows a picture of elders pouring libation to pray to God and ancestors. Which type of worship does this represent?
hints: Think of the indigenous worship practiced before foreign religions came.
questions.explanation: Pouring libation and invoking ancestors and the Supreme Being is part of Traditional worship.

criteria.description: Identifies the act as Traditional worship.
Mentions that libation is a traditional practice.

questions.stem: Tell your partner where Christians usually go to hold their worship services.
hints: Think of the building with a cross or church sign.
questions.explanation: Christians typically worship in a church building or chapel.

criteria.description: Names church, chapel, or cathedral.

questions.stem: Tell your partner where Muslims gather for communal Friday prayers.
hints: Think of the holy building with a minaret.
questions.explanation: Muslims worship in a mosque (masjid).

criteria.description: Names a mosque or masjid.

questions.stem: Which worship setting is connected with shrines, sacred groves, or royal palaces in Ghana?
hints: Traditional priests and priestesses worship at shrines.
questions.explanation: Shrines and sacred spaces are common places for Traditional worship in Ghana.

questions.stem: Name two different places of worship you can see in Ghanaian communities.
hints: Think about churches, mosques, or traditional shrines.
questions.explanation: Learners identify two distinct worship locations such as a church, mosque, or shrine.

criteria.description: Names two distinct places of worship (e.g., church and mosque).

questions.stem: In pairs, demonstrate how people respectfully enter a place of worship, such as taking off shoes before stepping on prayer mats or sitting quietly in church.
hints: Show quiet, respectful movements.
questions.explanation: Role-playing respectful entry into a place of worship demonstrates cultural and religious reverence.

criteria.description: Demonstrates a respectful action (e.g. quiet behavior, removing footwear where required).
Explains which religious setting the action represents.

questions.stem: Why is it important to keep quiet and show respect when people are worshipping?
hints: Think about showing love and respect to God and neighbours.
questions.explanation: Worship is sacred communication with God, so showing quiet respect honours worshippers and their faith.

criteria.description: Explains that worship is a holy or sacred time.
Mentions being peaceful and not disturbing others.

questions.stem: Role-play with your group: Show a Christian prayer posture (e.g., closing eyes and folding hands) and an Islamic prayer posture (e.g., raising hands to ears in Takbir).
hints: Show one posture for each religion respectfully.
questions.explanation: Learners demonstrate familiarity with the distinct, respectful prayer postures of both religions.

criteria.description: Demonstrates a Christian prayer posture correctly and respectfully.
Demonstrates an Islamic prayer posture correctly and respectfully.

questions.stem: A child says, 'Only Christians pray to God; Muslims and Traditionalists do not worship God.' Explain how this statement is mistaken based on our RME lesson.
hints: All three religions worship God in their own way.
questions.explanation: In Ghana, all three main religions—Christianity, Islam, and African Traditional Religion—engage in worship and prayer to the Supreme Being.

criteria.description: Clarifies that all three religions worship and pray.
States that Ghana recognises Christian, Islamic, and Traditional worship.

questions.stem: Draw a picture of people going to worship on a holy day (such as Sunday or Friday). Tell your teacher which worship you drew.
hints: Show people dressed neatly going to church or mosque.
questions.explanation: Learners draw worshippers and explain the religion represented, demonstrating visual and conceptual understanding.

criteria.description: Draws worshippers visiting a place of worship.
Correctly names whether it is Christian, Islamic, or Traditional worship.

questions.stem: Your friend Kofi is a Christian, Amina is a Muslim, and Nana is from a Traditional home. How can all three live happily together in the same classroom?
hints: Think about respect, love, and being good friends.
questions.explanation: Living together peacefully requires respecting each other's beliefs, loving one another, and focusing on shared values.

criteria.description: Mentions mutual respect for different worship practices.
Suggests showing love, kindness, and friendship in school.

questions.stem: Create a short speech for your classmates explaining the three main types of worship in Ghana and why we should respect all of them.
hints: Name the three religions and give one reason for peace.
questions.explanation: The speech should name Christianity, Islam, and Traditional religion and advocate for peaceful coexistence.

criteria.description: Accurately names all three main types of worship.
Gives a sound reason for respecting everyone (e.g. unity, peace, love).

questions.stem: Act out a short scene where children from Christian, Islamic, and Traditional backgrounds greet each other politely on their way to worship.
hints: Show warm greetings and smiling faces.
questions.explanation: This role-play demonstrates positive interpersonal relationships across Ghana's religious landscape.

criteria.description: Represents children heading to their respective worship settings.
Demonstrates warm, respectful greetings and religious tolerance.

uncertain: The indicator code is printed as BI 2.1.1.1 in the curriculum and is preserved verbatim.

indicators.objective: Recite religious passages and sing religious songs.
indicators.content_standard_as_printed: B1.2.1.1. Demonstrate the understanding of religious worship
indicators.strand: Religious Practices and their Moral Implications
indicators.sub_strand: Religious Worship in the Three Major Religions in Ghana

skills.description: Identify specific passages, songs, and recitations belonging to the three main religions (e.g., Lord's Prayer, Psalm 23, Al-Fatihah, traditional proverbs/myths).
Recite or explain lines and meanings from sacred texts and songs of the three religions.
Explain moral lessons and comfort derived from singing religious songs and reciting sacred words.

misconceptions: Thinking Al-Fatihah is a Christian prayer
Thinking Psalm 23 or the Lord's Prayer is an Islamic recital
Believing traditional religion has no oral recitals, sacred proverbs, or songs

questions.stem: Which of these is a well-known Christian prayer taught in our lesson?
hints: It begins with 'Our Father who art in heaven'.
questions.explanation: The Lord's Prayer is a foundational Christian prayer listed in the curriculum.

distractor_misconceptions.1: Confusing an Islamic prayer with a Christian prayer
distractor_misconceptions.2: Confusing a traditional recital with a Christian prayer
distractor_misconceptions.3: Confusing a national song with a religious prayer

questions.stem: Which passage from the Bible begins with 'The Lord is my shepherd'?
hints: It is a famous Psalm of King David.
questions.explanation: Psalm 23 is the Christian passage that starts with 'The Lord is my shepherd'.

distractor_misconceptions.1: Confusing Quranic surahs with biblical psalms
distractor_misconceptions.2: Confusing a playground rhyme with sacred scripture
distractor_misconceptions.3: Confusing traditional proverbs with biblical psalms

questions.stem: Which of these is the opening chapter of the Holy Quran recited in Islamic worship?
hints: It is recited in every unit of Islamic prayer (Salat).
questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah is the opening Surah of the Quran, recited by Muslims in worship.

distractor_misconceptions.1: Confusing a Christian psalm with a Quranic recitation
distractor_misconceptions.2: Confusing the Lord's Prayer with Islamic recitation
distractor_misconceptions.3: Confusing folklore with sacred Quranic scripture

questions.stem: What type of religious recitations are handed down in African Traditional Religion through songs, riddles, myths, and ___?
hints: Elders use these short wise sayings to teach wisdom.
questions.explanation: The curriculum specifies sacred myths, riddles, and proverbs as traditional religious recitals.
questions.misconception: Believing traditional religion lacks oral wisdom and recitations

questions.stem: When Christians recite 'Give us this day our daily bread', which prayer are they saying?
hints: It asks God to provide daily food.
questions.explanation: 'Give us this day our daily bread' is a line from the Lord's Prayer.

distractor_misconceptions.1: Confusing the Lord's Prayer with Surah Al-Fatihah
distractor_misconceptions.2: Confusing a sacred Christian prayer with a traditional song
distractor_misconceptions.3: Confusing prayer with a marching band song

questions.stem: Recite the opening line of The Lord's Prayer for your teacher.
hints: 'Our Father...'
questions.explanation: Learners recite 'Our Father who art in heaven' (or local language equivalent).

criteria.description: Recites 'Our Father who art in heaven' accurately.

questions.stem: Recite the first verse of Psalm 23.
hints: 'The Lord is my shepherd...'
questions.explanation: Learners recite 'The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want.'

criteria.description: Recites 'The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want' (or equivalent translation).

questions.stem: Recite the opening words of Surah Al-Fatihah (Bismillah...).
hints: Bismillahir Rahmanir Raheem.
questions.explanation: Learners recite the Bismillah or opening verse of Surah Al-Fatihah.

criteria.description: Recites 'Bismillahir Rahmanir Raheem' or the opening of Al-Fatihah clearly.

questions.stem: Share one wise proverb or riddle from your home culture that teaches people to do good.
hints: Think of a saying your grandparents or elders tell you.
questions.explanation: Learners share an oral traditional proverb, riddle, or moral saying from their community.

criteria.description: States a relevant traditional proverb, riddle, or wise saying.
Briefly tells what good behavior it teaches.

questions.stem: In Psalm 23, what does the sheep say about the shepherd?
options: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want
The shepherd has lost his way
There is no grass in the valley
hints: The shepherd provides everything the sheep needs.
questions.explanation: Psalm 23 begins with trust: 'The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.'

distractor_misconceptions.1: Misinterpreting the psalm as showing confusion
distractor_misconceptions.2: Thinking of commercial sheep farming instead of spiritual care
distractor_misconceptions.3: Contradicting the psalm's green pastures imagery

questions.stem: What does 'Al-Rahman' and 'Al-Raheem' in Al-Fatihah teach Muslims about God (Allah)?
options: That God is Most Gracious and Most Merciful
That God wants people to quarrel
hints: Rahman and Raheem mean kindness and mercy.
questions.explanation: In Al-Fatihah, Allah is praised as the Most Gracious, Most Merciful.

questions.stem: Sing a short religious song you know from church, mosque, or community that praises God.
hints: Choose a simple chorus praising God.
questions.explanation: Learners sing an age-appropriate religious hymn, nasheed, or sacred chorus.

criteria.description: Sings a respectful song praising God.
Explains which religious tradition it belongs to.

questions.stem: In The Lord's Prayer, we say 'Forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.' What does this teach us to do when someone wrongs us?
hints: Think about not keeping anger in our hearts.
questions.explanation: This line teaches us to forgive others when they hurt us or make mistakes.

criteria.description: Explains that it teaches forgiveness and letting go of anger.
Connects it to being peaceful with classmates.

questions.stem: Why do believers feel comforted when they recite sacred words or sing songs during difficult times?
hints: Think about feeling that God is with them.
questions.explanation: Sacred recitations remind believers of God's love, protection, and care, bringing calm and hope.

criteria.description: Mentions feeling God's presence or protection.
Describes feeling calm, happy, or comforted.

questions.stem: An Akan proverb says: 'Tikoro nko agyina' (One head does not go into council). What does this traditional saying teach us?
options: We should cooperate and seek advice from others
We should always work completely alone
We should never listen to our parents
hints: Two heads are better than one.
questions.explanation: This traditional proverb teaches cooperation, collaboration, and listening to wise advice.

distractor_misconceptions.2: Assuming traditional sayings oppose parental guidance
distractor_misconceptions.3: Claiming one individual has all knowledge

questions.stem: Draw a picture of a child praying peacefully. Write or state one word that describes how the child feels (e.g., peace, love, joy).
hints: Show a calm and happy prayer posture.
questions.explanation: Learners represent prayer visually and express the emotional value of prayer.

criteria.description: Draws a child in a calm prayer posture.
Names a positive feeling associated with prayer (peace, comfort, joy).

questions.stem: How does singing together in school or at home help children become good friends?
hints: Singing brings people together in joy.
questions.explanation: Singing together fosters unity, shared joy, and love among children.

criteria.description: Explains that singing together builds unity or happiness.
Mentions that it helps children share and cooperate.

questions.stem: Lead your small group in reciting either The Lord's Prayer, Psalm 23, or Surah Al-Fatihah with reverence and clear voices.
hints: Stand or sit respectfully and recite together.
questions.explanation: Demonstrates leadership, respectful recitation, and teamwork.

criteria.description: Recites the chosen sacred passage accurately and reverently.
Encourages peers to participate respectfully.

questions.stem: Your friend is sad because of a problem. Which line from Psalm 23 or another prayer would you share to comfort them, and why?
hints: 'The Lord is my shepherd' or 'God is merciful'.
questions.explanation: Learners connect a specific sacred line to comforting someone in distress.

criteria.description: Quotes or recalls a comforting sacred phrase or concept.
Explains how it gives hope or encouragement.

questions.stem: Explain two ways sacred recitations and songs teach children to be honest, kind, and peaceful citizens.
hints: Think about what the prayers ask us to do every day.
questions.explanation: Learners explain that sacred texts instruct us to tell the truth, care for neighbours, and live in harmony.

criteria.description: Mentions moral lessons like honesty or forgiveness taught in prayers.
Explains how putting those words into action makes school and home peaceful.

uncertain: The indicator code is printed as BI 2.1.1.2 in the curriculum and is preserved verbatim.
